build_inputs.angles:
- Lead on this: Renault took a front-engine, front-wheel-drive economy hatchback and had TWR rebuild it as a mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive two-seater — hand-built in Uddevalla, Sweden, with the back seats replaced by a V6.
- Cover the rarity and the reputation: only about 1,500 Phase 1 cars were built, roughly as many as the Ferrari F40, and it earned a name for handling that would bite drivers who got it wrong.
- For the head-to-head use the Mk4 Volkswagen Golf R32 — the sensible way to put a V6 in a hatchback. Near-identical power and 0-60, front-engine and all-wheel drive, and today the Clio is worth about four times as much.

The Renault Clio V6 is powered by a 3.0-liter V6 engine, delivering 230 hp and 221 lb-ft of torque, making it a compact powerhouse. Inside, the Clio V6 features suede-covered steering and Renaultsport seats, emphasizing its sporty character. This Clio earned a reputation for its challenging handling—catching out drivers who underestimated its demands. The Clio V6’s dual exhausts integrated into the rear bumper highlight its aggressive and performance-oriented appearance. They go for about $90,000 today, holding their value remarkably well compared to standard models. sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2001 Renault Clio V6, finished in Iceberg Silver with a blue and gray interior, and will be displayed live at Willow Springs Reimagined as part of the Cars & Bids Willow Springs Collection. This Renault is a Japanese-market, left-hand-drive hatchback currently titled in Washington state and located in California. Badged the "Lutécia V6" for the Japanese market, this Clio V6 is equipped with a metric instrument cluster, and the odometer currently displays approximately 30,300 kilometers, or approximately 19,000 miles. A partial list of notable equipment reported by the selling dealer includes 17-inch wheels, a Clio V6-specific body kit, leather and synthetic suede upholstery, front sport seats, and a CD player. The selling dealer reports no notable modifications. Born from the Clio V6 Trophy race car, the road-going Renault Clio V6 arrived in 2001 as one of Renault Sport's most ambitious creations. For the "Phase 1" Clio V6, TWR transformed the humble front-engine, front-wheel-drive Clio into a wide-bodied, mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive two-seater, with each example hand-built in Uddevalla, Sweden. Its exotic layout, dramatic proportions, and famously demanding handling made it unlike virtually anything else on sale -- and its appearances in mid-'00s media like Top Gear, Need for Speed, and plenty more helped establish the Clio V6 as a modern Renault icon even in parts of the world where it was never originally sold. Power comes from a 3.0-liter V6, rated at 230 horsepower and 221 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 6-speed manual transmission.
